name: Chris Backemeyer
current_role: Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State
bio: Chris Backemeyer is the Democratic nominee for Nebraska's 1st congressional district, born and raised in Lincoln and a graduate of Lincoln East High School. He joined the State Department after 9/11 and worked on counterterrorism, economic policy and the Middle East under administrations of both parties, rising to deputy assistant secretary. He also served on the White House National Security Council and advised the Office of the Vice President.

platform.point: Create a public option for universal coverage, extend ACA premium tax credits and lower the Medicare eligibility age to 60.
Expand the Child Tax Credit and rebalance the tax code so billionaires and corporations pay more.
Roll back tariffs he says hurt Nebraska farmers and have Congress reclaim authority over tariffs.
Pass comprehensive reform with a pathway to citizenship, cut excess ICE funding and keep strong southern border security.
Keep a strong defense and alliances while reasserting congressional war powers; criticizes the Iran war strategy.
Pass a long-term Farm Bill, allow year-round E15 sales and break up agribusiness monopolies.
Term limits for Congress and judges, a congressional stock-trading ban and overturning Citizens United.
Protect abortion rights in Nebraska and nationwide.

economy.evidence: Wants billionaires and corporations to pay more tax, an expanded Child Tax Credit and agribusiness antitrust, while opposing tariffs and housing red tape.

welfare.evidence: Proposes a public option to guarantee universal coverage, Medicare eligibility at 60 and restored Medicaid funding.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only: pledges to protect a woman's right to choose in Nebraska and nationwide; no positions found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

immigration.evidence: Backs a pathway to citizenship, clawing back about $75 billion in ICE funding and limits on detention expansion, alongside strong border security.

foreign.evidence: Calls for a strong defense and stronger alliances through diplomacy, but also for congressional war powers to avoid forever wars.

notes: Read each campaign priority page plus Norfolk Daily News coverage (April and August 2026); Lincoln Journal Star pages were behind a gateway, and no positions were found on policing, energy, tech, schools or religion. The Commons file title misspells the surname as Backemyer, but its source is his State Department biography.

name: Carmen Bucco
bio: Carmen Bucco owns a tailoring business and founded the charitable foundation Bucco's Rising Stars, and is a former Belleville school board member. Bucco was the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 10th district in both the 2024 special and regular elections and has also run for county and state legislative offices. The campaign biography describes a childhood that included foster care and periods of homelessness.

platform.point: Supports police and first responders and opposes restrictions that limit law enforcement.
Wants to control government spending, cut waste and ease the cost of living.
Proposes reducing regulatory burdens and loan barriers for small businesses.
Pledges to hold public officials accountable and root out political corruption.
Calls for a return to academic fundamentals, safer schools and more trade education.
Calls for real support systems to address the mental health crisis.
Wants to limit overdevelopment to protect homeowners from rising property taxes.
Says no one, including Trump, tells the candidate how to vote.

economy.evidence: Calls for controlling spending, eliminating waste and reducing regulations on small businesses.

welfare.evidence: General statement: wants to end fraud so that taxpayer money reaches vulnerable people who need help.

liberty.evidence: On guns, backs Second Amendment rights for self-protection; no positions found on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech.

security.evidence: Opposes restrictions on police and supports a tough-on-crime approach.

notes: Read the campaign home, about, message and issues pages and New Jersey Globe coverage; on an August 2026 detainee death at Delaney Hall the candidate urged against politicizing it but stated no immigration policy. Nothing found on immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion, and the education plank does not address school choice.

name: Michael McGuire
current_role: Family law attorney and Marine Corps veteran
bio: Michael McGuire is a family law attorney from Freehold Township and the Republican nominee for New Jersey's 3rd District, having won a three-way primary in June 2026. He is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran serving in the Navy Reserve and is a retired New York City police officer. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Cut wasteful federal spending, burdensome regulations and taxes on middle- and working-class families.
Signed a pledge to support term limits for members of Congress.
Supports banning stock trading by members of Congress.
Prioritize military readiness, training and modernization.
Improve the VA and ensure veterans can access health care, including mental health services.
Campaign describes a commitment to protecting the unborn and to parental rights.
Wants to enhance public safety so people feel safe in their homes.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting wasteful spending, burdensome regulations and taxes on middle-class families.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only, general statement: his campaign cites a commitment to protecting the unborn, without naming specific legislation; nothing found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

security.evidence: General statement: pledges to enhance public safety; he is a retired NYPD officer.

foreign.evidence: Prioritizes military readiness, training and modernization.

notes: Read the campaign issues, about and news pages from the site map plus New Jersey Globe and Pine Barrens Tribune coverage; the May 2026 primary debate and an April 2026 Newsmax interview on Iran are video-only and were not reviewed. Nothing found on immigration, energy, tech, schools or religion, and the campaign image is a wide banner rather than a headshot.

name: Sean Kirrane
bio: Sean Kirrane is a corporate consultant and artificial intelligence entrepreneur from River Vale and the Republican nominee in New Jersey's 5th District. He moved to New Jersey from Oklahoma, has not held elected office, and cites experience in the health care and business sectors. He describes himself as a socially moderate, fiscally responsible Republican.

platform.point: Create a universal, market-based health plan funded through income-based taxes with cost-sharing, not single-payer.
Pass sweeping affordable housing legislation driven by the private market.
Impose lifetime lobbying bans on former members of Congress.
Focus on lowering health care costs and improving outcomes.

economy.evidence: General self-description as fiscally responsible, plus a preference for private-market housing solutions.

welfare.evidence: Proposes a universal health care system funded through the tax system on an income basis, though market-run.

notes: The campaign site is a client-side app with no readable issue text (its script bundles hold no policy copy), no campaign social accounts were found, and NJ Spotlight blocked access. Only New Jersey Globe coverage from 2025-2026 gave positions; he calls himself socially moderate but named no specific social issues.

name: Rebecca Bennett
current_role: Healthcare executive and Air National Guard officer
bio: Rebecca Bennett is a healthcare business executive and the Democratic nominee in New Jersey's 7th District. She flew helicopters in the U.S. Navy for over a decade as an aircraft commander and experimental test pilot, and now serves as an officer in the Air National Guard. She holds an MBA from the Wharton School and has worked with startups and Fortune 50 companies.

platform.point: Increase housing supply, fully restore the SALT deduction and pass paid family leave.
Reverse Medicaid and Medicare cuts, protect pre-existing condition coverage and expand youth mental health services.
Get military-style weapons off the streets, reinstate the silencer tax and restore CDC gun research funding.
Restore federal abortion rights and pass the Equality Act for LGBTQ+ protections.
Pass meaningful federal AI legislation instead of a state-by-state patchwork.
Opposes continued military operations against Iran and says she wants no more forever wars.
Support unions and the right to organize and strengthen fair wage and labor laws.
Keep pollution rules, incentivize solar and electric vehicles and upgrade the power grid.

economy.evidence: Backs union rights, stronger wage and labor laws and paid family leave, while also seeking a full SALT tax deduction and less housing red tape.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to reverse Medicaid and Medicare cuts, pass paid family leave and fully fund elder care.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: restore federal abortion rights; LGBTQ: pass the Equality Act; guns: take military-style weapons off the streets and reinstate the silencer tax.

security.evidence: General statement: wants local police to have the resources they need while building trust with the communities they serve.

foreign.evidence: Wants to counter China and remain a reliable partner abroad, but opposes the Iran war and forever wars.

energy.evidence: Calls for keeping environmental regulations and incentivizing solar, electric vehicles and renewable energy to address climate change.

tech.evidence: Calls for meaningful national AI legislation and for holding social media companies accountable for harmful practices.

notes: Read all eight campaign priority pages and September 2026 New Jersey Globe coverage; on immigration she mentions only bipartisan reform, and nothing was found on schools or religion. The campaign image is a screenshot file that may not be a formal headshot.

name: Nellie Pou
bio: Nellie Pou has represented New Jersey's 9th congressional district since January 2025 and serves on the House Homeland Security and Transportation and Infrastructure committees. She previously served in the New Jersey General Assembly from 1997 to 2012 and the State Senate from 2012 to 2025. She was born in Paterson.

platform.point: Focuses on lowering housing, grocery, childcare and healthcare costs for New Jersey families.
Wants to protect the ACA, extend its tax credits, lower drug prices and safeguard Medicaid coverage.
Introduced the Crime Gun Tracing Modernization Act to let the ATF search gun-trace records electronically.
Introduced the PLATE Act to bar ICE agents from hiding or altering vehicle license plates.
Voted for the Ukraine Support Act to fund Ukraine and sanction Russia.
Voted for a resolution to end hostilities with Iran absent a declaration of war.
Opposed the 2025 tariffs on Canada and Mexico as raising the cost of living.
Demanded restoration of $7.9 million in community school grants cut from Passaic County schools.

welfare.evidence: Backs protecting the ACA and Medicaid and extending ACA premium tax credits.

liberty.evidence: Guns only: sponsored the Crime Gun Tracing Modernization Act to lift limits on ATF electronic trace searches; no record reviewed on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech.

security.evidence: Supports funding for law enforcement and community safety as a Homeland Security Committee member.

immigration.evidence: Voted against the Laken Riley Act, sponsored the PLATE Act on ICE vehicles and criticized expanded immigration detention.

foreign.evidence: Voted for the Ukraine Support Act's aid and Russia sanctions, while also voting to end Iran hostilities without congressional authorization.

tech.evidence: Voted for the TAKE IT DOWN Act on nonconsensual intimate images, which passed 409-2.

education.evidence: Pressed the Education Department to restore $7.9 million in cut federal grants to Paterson and Passaic public schools.

faith.evidence: Led 27 lawmakers asking DHS to provide religious accommodations such as prayer space, Qurans and halal meals to Muslim ICE detainees.

notes: Reviewed campaign priorities, House press releases and House Clerk roll calls (Laken Riley Act, H.R. 1, TAKE IT DOWN Act); economy is left null because she voted against H.R. 1 but also opposes tariffs, and her state legislative record on abortion could not be retrieved. The official social accounts listed in the input appear to belong to House administrative offices, so only campaign accounts are recorded.

name: Didi Okpareke
bio: Ndidiamaka "Didi" Okpareke is a pharmacist who founded Olive Tree Compounding Pharmacy in 2016. The daughter of Nigerian immigrants, she has lived in the Albuquerque area since 1997, attended Sandia High School and earned her pharmacy degree at UNM. She is the 2026 Republican nominee in NM-1.

platform.point: Make health care affordable and accessible, lower pharmacy costs and keep rural pharmacies open.
Bring federal investment and programs to New Mexico to create jobs and raise pay.
Encourage entrepreneurship, investment and less state reliance on federal aid.
Says New Mexico businesses are burdened by overregulation.
Address the state's low education rankings and high crime.
Promises to answer to New Mexicans rather than party leaders in Washington.

economy.evidence: General statement: says businesses are burdened by overregulation, though her site also promises to seek federal investment for jobs.

welfare.evidence: General statement: wants New Mexico to focus on self-sufficiency and less reliance on federal aid.

faith.evidence: General statement: pledges to protect faith, family and freedom, and her campaign biography stresses faith in God.

notes: Found the campaign site and social accounts; the site's single page and 2025 launch coverage (NM Political Report, Piñon Post) give only general themes. Nothing found on immigration, abortion, guns, energy, foreign policy, tech or school choice, and Source NM and Santa Fe New Mexican pages were blocked or rate-limited.

name: Greg Cunningham
current_role: Retired police detective and business owner
bio: Greg Cunningham is a lifelong New Mexican and Marine Corps veteran who served as a field radio operator. He worked about 20 years with the Albuquerque Police Department, retiring as a detective, and later owned a private investigations business. He ran for the New Mexico House in 2022 and 2024 and is the 2026 Republican nominee in NM-2, with an endorsement from President Trump.

platform.point: Pledges to stand with President Trump in closing down the border.
Opposes efforts to defund the police and wants violent criminals locked up.
Defends the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's Medicaid changes and wants to root out ineligible enrollment.
Wants to ease burdens on small businesses and help create good-paying jobs.
Pressed the administration to halt new border-wall contractor wells in drought-stricken Luna County.
Calls for holding the education system accountable.
Promises commonsense, conservative-guided solutions that put people over politics.

economy.evidence: General statement: wants to ease the burdens on small businesses.

welfare.evidence: Defends Medicaid changes in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and stresses eligibility checks.

security.evidence: General statements: opposes defunding the police and prioritizes locking up violent criminals and holding offenders accountable.

immigration.evidence: General statement: pledges to stand with President Trump in closing down the border.

faith.evidence: General statement: names faith, family and freedom as core values and says his faith guides his work.

notes: The campaign site has only a home page; positions come from Santa Fe New Mexican, Searchlight NM and NM Political Report coverage, and a June 2026 podcast on tariffs, taxes and Iran was audio/video only. Nothing specific found on abortion, guns, energy, foreign policy, tech or schools; an October 16 debate with Vasquez is scheduled.
